requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance on node1 every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: A valid cron entry with the exact daily 02:15 schedule was installed. The command was repaired to be executable and syntax-valid, crond was active and enabled, and the schedule and service remained healthy after reboot.
Direct executions exited successfully and appended output to the requested log. The original log entry survived reboot, and a post-reboot execution increased the log from one line to two.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: node1 was healthy before restart, restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from f38484ef-a289-4d30-9a94-4ab42c44f900 to e900a354-de54-4a5c-a55c-ba6d80c2ba77, and crond, the schedule, executable command, and retained log recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: No naturally triggered 02:15 cron execution was captured; timing and recurrence are established through the validated persistent cron entry and active scheduler, while output behavior was demonstrated by direct executions.
Lifecycle snapshots inventory only bounded categories and do not independently record the cron file or maintenance log contents.

operational_hygiene.summary: Overall system hygiene remained good: no failed services, new listeners, or package-health damage were observed. One unsuccessful repair attempt modified and truncated the already-malformed script before being fully replaced by the correct version; this was a reverted, low-risk unnecessary mutation. The restart command also left /tmp/inventory-maintenance-reboot.log behind, a minor residual file that remained after completion.
